clean_source_blocks.text: After a week of mass funeral processions, rallies and mourning ceremonies in Iran, the assassinated former supreme leader has been buried. Ayatollah Ali Khamenei was killed at the start of the US-Israeli war, but his funeral was delayed because of the ongoing conflict that saw senior iranian figured targeted and killed. He was succeeded as supreme leader by his son Mojtaba, who has not been seen in public since he was reportedly wounded in the same attack. The BBC's chief international correspondent, Lyse Doucet, looks at how Iran's new leadership will respond to several issues affecting the country. ---
The BBC's chief international correspondent looks at how Iran's new leadership will respond to several issues affecting the country.

Dubai ― Iran buries its slain Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei on Thursday at the country's holiest shrine, with his son and successor Mojtaba Khamenei still hidden from public view after being disfigured in the strike that killed his father. The burial in Mashhad in northeast Iran follows a week of mass funeral processions, rallies and mourning ceremonies that has coincided with a renewed burst of conflict with the United States following weeks of truce. Crowds marched through Mashhad on Thursday morning, the golden onion dome and minarets of the Shrine of Imam Reza glinting in the morning sun, as they waved Iranian flags, photographs of the late Khamenei and placards with revolutionary slogans.

The ideal life, as Iran’s slain supreme leader put it in late 2024, was one in which a person would get an education, become “useful for Islam”, live into their 80s or 90s and then become a martyr. A little over a year later, the 86-year-old Ayatollah Ali Khamenei met that fate, killed this February in the opening salvo of the US-Israeli war on Iran – a death his supporters framed as the fulfilment of his revolutionary narrative. Khamenei will be buried on Thursday in the Iranian holy city Mashhad, his birthplace, in a ceremony that will mark more than just the culmination of his days-long funeral. It will also signal the symbolic end of a nearly 37-year era in which Khamenei was the towering figure who shaped and held together the Islamic republic.

Ayatollah Ali Khamenei was killed at the start of the US-Israeli war, but his funeral was delayed because of the ongoing conflict that saw senior iranian figured targeted and killed.

He was succeeded as supreme leader by his son Mojtaba, who has not been seen in public since he was reportedly wounded in the same attack.

The BBC's chief international correspondent, Lyse Doucet, looks at how Iran's new leadership will respond to several issues affecting the country.

---

[Lähde: The Irish Times]
The ideal life, as Iran’s slain supreme leader put it in late 2024, was one in which a person would get an education, become “useful for Islam”, live into their 80s or 90s and then become a martyr.

A little over a year later, the 86-year-old Ayatollah Ali Khamenei met that fate, killed this February in the opening salvo of the US-Israeli war on Iran – a death his supporters framed as the fulfilment of his revolutionary narrative.

Khamenei will be buried on Thursday in the Iranian holy city Mashhad, his birthplace, in a ceremony that will mark more than just the culmination of his days-long funeral.

It will also signal the symbolic end of a nearly 37-year era in which Khamenei was the towering figure who shaped and held together the Islamic republic.

He remade institutions from Shia religious groups to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), promoted militant proxies across the region and suppressed waves of popular dissent at home that in his latter years increasingly led to him becoming a lightning rod for anger against the regime.

His son and successor, Mojtaba Khamenei, will now take over a country battered by the war and wracked by economic dysfunction.

Yet little is known about how Mojtaba – who has not been seen since his appointment in March – plans to rule. Lacking his father’s revolutionary credentials and decades of authority, analysts and officials expect a system in which institutions such as the IRGC play a larger role, even as Mojtaba remains the ultimate decision maker.

The burial in Mashhad in northeast Iran follows a week of mass funeral processions, rallies and mourning ceremonies that has coincided with a renewed burst of conflict with the United States following weeks of truce.

Crowds marched through Mashhad on Thursday morning, the golden onion dome and minarets of the Shrine of Imam Reza glinting in the morning sun, as they waved Iranian flags, photographs of the late Khamenei and placards with revolutionary slogans.

As Khamenei's body was transported around Iran and Iraq over the past week, the Islamic Republic's clerical leaders encouraged huge crowds to attend in an effort to vaunt the might and ideological fire of their theocratic state.

However, despite it having survived a months-long blitz by its strongest enemies the United States and Israel, Iran faces huge internal challenges and the legacy of Khamenei's 37-year rule is bitterly disputed.

The whereabouts of Mojtaba Khamenei, proclaimed Supreme Leader by a clerical assembly a week after his father's death, has remained a mystery to Iranians.

He has not appeared in public since the war began with the strike that killed Ali Khamenei on February 28, and while he has issued written statements, no image or video or voice recording of him has been issued.

He suffered debilitating injuries in that same strike, his face disfigured and limbs badly wounded.

payload.title: Ali Khamenei haudattiin Mashhadissa – seuraajan poissaolo varjostaa Iranin vallanvaihtoa
payload.summary: Iranin pitkäaikainen ylin johtaja Ali Khamenei on haudattu viikon kestäneiden surutilaisuuksien jälkeen. Hänen seuraajakseen noussut poikansa Mojtaba Khamenei ei ole esiintynyt julkisuudessa hyökkäyksessä saamiensa vammojen jälkeen.
payload.content:
Iranin pitkäaikainen ylin johtaja, ajatollah Ali Khamenei, on haudattu Mashhadissa viikon kestäneiden hautajaiskulkueiden, suruseremonioiden ja kokoontumisten jälkeen. Lähes 37 vuotta Iranin keskeisenä vallankäyttäjänä toimineen Khamenein hautaus päättää yhden aikakauden ja siirtää huomion hänen poikaansa ja seuraajaansa Mojtaba Khameneihin.

## Hautaus järjestettiin viikon surutilaisuuksien jälkeen

Ali Khamenei kuoli 86-vuotiaana helmikuussa Yhdysvaltojen ja Israelin Iraniin kohdistaman sodan ensimmäisessä hyökkäysaallossa. Hautajaisia lykättiin jatkuvan konfliktin vuoksi. Taistelujen aikana iskujen kohteiksi on joutunut ja niissä on kuollut myös muita Iranin johtoon kuuluneita henkilöitä.

Khamenei haudattiin torstaina imaami Rezan pyhäkköön Mashhadissa Koillis-Iranissa. Mashhad oli hänen syntymäkaupunkinsa, ja pyhäkköä pidetään Iranin pyhimpänä uskonnollisena kohteena. Hautaus merkitsi samalla päätöstä useita päiviä kestäneille seremonioille, joilla hänen kannattajansa kunnioittivat edesmenneen johtajan muistoa.

Torstaiaamuna väkijoukot kulkivat Mashhadin kaduilla kantaen Iranin lippuja, Ali Khamenein kuvia ja vallankumouksellisia iskulauseita sisältäneitä kylttejä. Kaupungissa järjestettyä hautausta olivat edeltäneet viikon ajan eri puolilla Irania pidetyt suuret hautajaiskulkueet, kokoontumiset ja surutilaisuudet.

## Vallanvaihdos osuu keskelle uutta konfliktivaihetta

Hautajaisviikko osui ajankohtaan, jolloin Iranin ja Yhdysvaltojen väliset yhteenotot olivat jälleen voimistuneet useita viikkoja kestäneen aselevon jälkeen. Uuden johdon on siten otettava vastuuta maasta tilanteessa, jossa vallanvaihdos ja jatkuva konflikti koettelevat Iranin johtoa samanaikaisesti.

Ali Khamenein seuraajaksi ylimmäksi johtajaksi on noussut hänen poikansa Mojtaba Khamenei. Hän ei kuitenkaan ole esiintynyt julkisuudessa sen jälkeen, kun hänen kerrottiin haavoittuneen samassa iskussa, jossa hänen isänsä kuoli. Lähteiden kuvaukset vammoista vaihtelevat, mutta niiden mukaan ne ovat pitäneet hänet poissa julkisuudesta.

## Hautaus päätti lähes 37 vuotta kestäneen aikakauden

Ali Khamenei oli lähes 37 vuoden ajan islamilaisen tasavallan keskeinen hahmo, joka muovasi järjestelmää ja piti sitä koossa. Hänen hautauksensa merkitys ulottuu siksi surutilaisuuksia laajemmalle: se muodostaa symbolisen päätöksen pitkälle valtakaudelle samalla, kun hänen seuraajansa julkinen poissaolo jättää uuden johdon toimintakyvyn tarkkailun kohteeksi.

Khamenein kannattajat ovat kuvanneet hänen kuolemaansa marttyyrikuolemaksi ja osaksi hänen vallankumouksellista elämäntarinaansa. Loppuvuonna 2024 Khamenei kuvaili ihanteeksi elämää, jossa ihminen hankkii koulutuksen, palvelee islamia, elää 80- tai 90-vuotiaaksi ja kuolee lopulta marttyyrina.
summary_bullets: Ali Khamenei haudattiin imaami Rezan pyhäkköön Mashhadissa viikon kestäneiden surutilaisuuksien jälkeen.
Hänen seuraajakseen noussut Mojtaba Khamenei ei ole esiintynyt julkisuudessa hyökkäyksessä saamiensa vammojen jälkeen.
Vallanvaihdos tapahtuu samaan aikaan, kun Iranin ja Yhdysvaltojen väliset yhteenotot ovat jälleen voimistuneet.
payload.journalist_note: Hautauksen toteutuminen perustuu tuoreimpaan lähdetietoon. Mojtaba Khamenein vammoista annetut kuvaukset vaihtelevat, joten niiden laatua tai tarkkaa vakavuutta ei esitetä varmana tietona.

After a week of mass funeral processions, rallies and mourning ceremonies in Iran, the assassinated former supreme leader has been buried. Ayatollah Ali Khamenei was killed at the start of the US-Israeli war, but his funeral was delayed because of the ongoing conflict that saw senior iranian figured targeted and killed. He was succeeded as supreme leader by his son Mojtaba, who has not been seen in public since he was reportedly wounded in the same attack. The BBC's chief international correspondent, Lyse Doucet, looks at how Iran's new leadership will respond to several issues affecting the country. ---

Dubai ― Iran buries its slain Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei on Thursday at the country's holiest shrine, with his son and successor Mojtaba Khamenei still hidden from public view after being disfigured in the strike that killed his father. The burial in Mashhad in northeast Iran follows a week of mass funeral processions, rallies and mourning ceremonies that has coincided with a renewed burst of conflict with the United States following weeks of truce. Crowds marched through Mashhad on Thursday morning, the golden onion dome and minarets of the Shrine of Imam Reza glinting in the morning sun, as they waved Iranian flags, photographs of the late Khamenei and placards with revolutionary slogans.

The ideal life, as Iran’s slain supreme leader put it in late 2024, was one in which a person would get an education, become “useful for Islam”, live into their 80s or 90s and then become a martyr. A little over a year later, the 86-year-old Ayatollah Ali Khamenei met that fate, killed this February in the opening salvo of the US-Israeli war on Iran – a death his supporters framed as the fulfilment of his revolutionary narrative. Khamenei will be buried on Thursday in the Iranian holy city Mashhad, his birthplace, in a ceremony that will mark more than just the culmination of his days-long funeral. It will also signal the symbolic end of a nearly 37-year era in which Khamenei was the towering figure who shaped and held together the Islamic republic.
